narrative: Left-endpoint Ito integral and the missing second-order term
GBM log transform and exact solution
OU integrating factor, conditional moments and stationary distribution
Euler approximation on shared Brownian increments
Normal generation and correlated Gaussian innovations

notation.state: Y for general state, S for GBM price, r for OU rate
notation.OU: kappa and theta map source gamma and r-bar

assumptions: Ito interpretation; nonanticipating integrands and square integrability when invoking zero expectation
C1 in time and C2 in state for the displayed Ito formula
Gaussian increments are independent across disjoint time intervals
GBM has positive initial price and constant mu/sigma; density formula requires sigma>0 and elapsed time>0
OU kappa>0 and constant theta,kappa,sigma_r; stationary density requires sigma_r>0
General density equations require appropriate regularity, density existence and boundary conditions
Correlated pair is formed from independent standard Gaussian base shocks; rho in [-1,1]
All data illustrative, no market calibration, physical/risk-neutral equivalence, or implied option valuation
clarifications: Finite Gaussian squared increment is dt*Z^2, not identically dt; coin construction differs
Left sum on finite grid equals .5*(W_T^2-Q_N), with limit .5*(W_T^2-T)
OU finite-time moments are derived additions to source integrating-factor solution
State-dependent forward coefficients remain inside derivatives
Euler may be nonpositive; do not clamp; even sigma=0 Euler differs from exponential exact growth when mu!=0
Sum of twelve uniforms minus six is bounded Normal approximation
Normal marginal laws alone do not guarantee jointly Gaussian variables; weighted variance includes covariance
Do not restore removed spreadsheet exercise

quadratic_variation.coupling: Aggregate same fine increments for every resolution

gbm_euler.coupling: Exact and Euler use same nested Brownian increments; no nonpositive clamp

correlation.sampling: Same independent base pairs reused when rho changes
correlation.display: All pairs included; sample variance denominator n-1; sample correlation calculated from centered shocks

random_generation.javascript: Existing seeded normalGenerator in src/math.mjs, Box-Muller transform of seeded uniforms; no new third-party sampler
random_generation.python: Python standard-library random.Random.gauss; seeds explicit in each Notebook cell
random_generation.cross_language: Experiments are independently reproducible; same numeric seed does not imply identical streams across languages
